neighbours.label: Sentence-final period (or clause comma / 'when') after a clause about a person, esp. a professional or client in a person-to-person interaction, where the next sentence will continue about that person with a pronoun

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, census arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + concept-census evidence (which concepts and domains selected the pole)); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Peak tokens are mostly '.' (50% coverage) at the end of sentences narrating one person's contact with another (client, banker, rabbi, referee), with a few ' when' and commas; output side suppresses ' him'/' them' (the + pole fires on the verb/preposition before an object pronoun for a person). Census says professions in neutral frames drive it, so the label stresses person-centered context, but much of the band mass is ordinary sentence-final periods, so this may be a weak, broad pole.
